verdict.reasoning: Patient reports watery diarrhea for about three days and nearly hourly when awake: "it's like basically I think it's diarrhoea... super watery" and "I feel like it's like almost every hour, when I'm awake" and "it's been about three days now."

Patient describes crampy abdominal pain low and midline, intermittent, and about 6–7/10: "it's like at the bottom... it feels pretty like in the middle"; "it comes and goes"; and "maybe is that like a six, or a seven?" which occurs before needing the toilet: "I feel, I feel a cramp... and then I know it's time to go."
When asked about blood in stools, patient denies it: "no I don't, I don't remember anything, like, no I , I think it's just I, nothing like that. There's nothing like that."

Patient reports nausea and vomiting, worse with milk: "yeah I definitely feel kind of nauseous... I've have vomited" and "whenever I have like milk or something like that, I just feel like I want to vomit. And actually, yeah one time I just like had some milk, and I just completely vomited it."
Patient feels hot but has not measured temperature: "I feel kind of really hot all the time... I'm pretty sure I'm burning up... I haven't actually done any temperature reading."
Patient notes passing urine less often: "yeah a bit, I guess less frequently maybe. Um but yeah, it seems to be OK."

Patient is drinking but feels fluids pass straight through: "I'm trying to drink a lot of water" and later "it just feels like the, the fluids do go down. But it just feels like it's going straight through."

Brother had similar illness about 5 days and seems to be improving: "my brother has had, actually had something like this for um he has it as well for five days" and "I think he's getting better, but I'm not, I'm not really sure."
Patient denies other medical history: "I think otherwise I'm fit and well" and "I can't think of any related medical history... no I I don't think so."
Patient uses paracetamol but no regular meds: "I've been taking some like Paracetamols and stuff like that lately. But uh, I haven't been, I'm not on any regular medication or anything like that."
Patient reports no known allergies: "I don't have any allergies that I know of."
Patient states father has colon cancer and describes it as third stage: "my, my dad actually has um colon cancer at the moment" and "he's sort of in his third stage."
Living situation and job match: "I live with my, um sister and my mum" and "I work at um an office, um in Central London. Um it's uh, so I work in government."

Patient smokes socially and occasionally drinks heavily: "I smoke... socially, but not like regularly... if it's a Friday or something like that I might have a cigarette" and for alcohol "once or twice a month, that yeah, I'll go out with my friends and drink a lot."

Doctor diagnoses gastroenteritis and notes high fluid loss; frequent stools imply dehydration risk: "your symptoms are suggestive of something called gastroenteritis" and "you're losing a lot of... fluid" and discussion of fluid replacement (Dioralyte) due to concern about minerals/vitamins.

Mild dehydration is a reasonable inference from "less frequently" passing urine and feeling very hot; doctor expresses concern about dehydration: "if you are getting dehydrated then we need to do further investigations."
Family history of colorectal cancer recorded: "my, my dad actually has um colon cancer at the moment" and doctor: "I'll make a not of that 'cause uh, important to know these kind of details."

Doctor advises Dioralyte but does not mention targeting pale yellow urine: "you can get things like Diarolyte, which is um, a fluid replacement you can get from the pharmacy"; there is no statement about aiming for pale yellow urine.
Doctor advises clear fluids and soft diet like soup and mash: "clear fluids. You can use soft diet, things like soup, mash. And then gradually build up, um as much as your body can tolerate."

Paracetamol as needed is recommended: "You can try just you know regular Paracetamol if you are feeling feverish" and later "If you are having, if you've got a bit of tummy pain, if you're feeling feverish, then I think Paracetamol is very sensible."
Doctor advises avoiding alcohol but does not advise avoiding dairy: "Try and avoid alcohol if you can." No instruction is given to avoid dairy products despite milk aggravating symptoms.

Doctor only specifies follow-up if not settling in 48 hours or concern for dehydration; no explicit red-flag list or fever threshold is given: "if your symptoms aren't settling down in the next couple of days, so forty eight hours, I want you to give me a call back" and "if you are getting dehydrated then we need to do further investigations." No mention of bloody stool, persistent vomiting, inability to keep fluids down, worsening pain, or fever over 38°C.

Follow-up by phone in 48 hours if not improving is clearly stated: "if your symptoms aren't settling down in the next couple of days, so forty eight hours, I want you to give me a call back" and "let's see how you are in the next one to two days."
